标题: Scalable Physics-Informed Neural Network for Real-Time Thermal Analysis for Battery Packs
作者: Shantanu Sarkar, Yoganathan Lakshmanan, Raju A.
原始摘要:
Accurately predicting Thermal and Flow parameters in Battery Pack Thermal Management System is very important to ensure maximum system efficiency, long range and vehicle safety. Traditionally, conventional Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) methods are used to get detailed insights into these parameters. But these methods remain computationally very expensive, which limits their application in real-time predictions. This study presents an alternate structured simulation framework that combines CFD fundamentals with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to enable fast and efficient prediction of thermal and flow behavior. PINNs incorporates the governing partial differential equations (PDEs) - mass, momentum and energy – directly into the neural network's loss function, enabling efficient learning with limited dependency on training datasets.
In this study, we present a PINN framework trained on limited datasets derived from general CFD simulations of flow and Conjugate Heat Transfer (CHT) cases for a battery pack. The trained PINN model is then validated against a separate set of test datasets obtained from independent studies, across key performance parameters including pressure drop, velocity, temperature distribution, and hotspot location. Comparative analysis indicates that the proposed PINN framework predicts key parameters within 5% deviation from test dataset values. The PINN model also significantly reduces computational time from 5-8 hours per case for traditional detailed CFD to 2-3 seconds. Additionally, the PINN framework requires only a closed-volume CAD geometry and does not rely on 3D-mesh. Limited data can be used to speed up the training process, thereby eliminating the time associated with pre-processing, repeated model setup for different cases, and subsequent corrections. Findings from this study demonstrate PINNs as a potential surrogate modelling tool for real-time thermal monitoring and rapid design iteration in battery cooling systems. This reduces dependency on computationally expensive simulations, thereby reducing development cycles and faster time for customers. This work shows a scalable physics-informed neural-network framework that can be extended beyond battery systems to other components at system and vehicle levels.

标题: Fatigue life prediction of variable-load industrial robotic arms based on physics-informed graph neural networks
原始摘要:
Introduction 
                     Industrial robotic arms operate under long-term variable-load conditions, and joint fatigue accumulation may lead to sudden failures. Conventional life-prediction methods cannot effectively integrate spatial topology, temporal degradation rules and fatigue physical mechanics. This study proposes a physics-informed Graph Attention-GRU (PI-GAT-GRU) model for fatigue-life prediction of variable-load industrial robotic arms. 
                   
                   
                     Methods 
                     Robotic-arm joints are mapped into a topology-mechanics graph. Spatiotemporal features are extracted via dynamic graph attention and GRU units. The Miner damage criterion and stiffness-degradation model are embedded, and a physics-regularized joint loss function is constructed for end-to-end fatigue-life prediction. Comparative experiments against three baseline models and ablation studies are conducted on multi-body simulation datasets covering low, medium and heavy-load conditions. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     The subset-level prediction accuracy of PI-GAT-GRU reaches 96%–97% under low-load, 94%–97% under medium-load, and 93%–95% under heavy-load conditions. Its overall average accuracy on the mixed full-condition test set is 92.48%. Benchmark models achieve 91%–94% accuracy under low-load and drop to 88%–92% under heavy-load conditions. The proposed model obtains better accuracy and robustness under variable-load scenarios. 
                   
                   
                     Discussion 
                     The PI-GAT-GRU realizes effective fusion of data-driven learning and fatigue physical constraints. It supplies reliable technical support for predictive maintenance and health management of industrial robotic arms. Further work will focus on cross-platform validation and nonlinear-damage mechanism integration.

标题: Deep Wavelet Diffeomorphism: A New Approach to Manifold Reshaping for PINN Training
作者: Shijiao Gao, Hanying Gao, Carlo Cattani, Shuli Mei
原始摘要: Abstract Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are a mesh-free, data-driven approach for solving partial differential equations (PDEs). However, their accuracy in capturing strong-gradient regions (such as shock waves) depends on dense, uniform collocation points, which can lead to convergence issues and susceptibility to local optima. Traditional adaptive wavelet solvers excel at identifying discontinuous regions but suffer from time-step constraints and require cumbersome threshold tuning. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Deep Wavelet Diffeomorphism (DWD) framework that integrates the strengths of both methods through a decoupled mechanism involving manifold regularization and low-dimensional training. Leveraging interpolating multiresolution analysis, DWD constructs a deep wavelet diffeomorphism that maps distorted physical-space training manifolds into smooth computational-space manifolds, while generating an optimal non-uniform collocation set---dense in feature-rich regions and sparse in smooth regions. This manifold mapping discretizes high-dimensional PDEs into a low-dimensional collocation system, which is then input into a standard PINN for efficient and stable optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that DWD achieves accuracy comparable to uniform super-resolution PINNs, while reducing collocation points by an order of magnitude and shortening training time by 5 to 8 times. It outperforms pure wavelet solvers and traditional PINNs in both accuracy and robustness. Concise and compatible with existing deep learning pipelines, DWD offers a data-efficient, low-dimensional discretization approach for high-dimensional PDEs and inverse problems in physics-informed learning.
